label: BEGINS_2: the time before every populated moment of a history is of finite duration
term: contingent concrete reality begins (finite duration of the time before populated moments)
definition: BEGINS_2. FiniteDurationBeginningAt h Concrete k v holds when some contingent concrete individual is present at some moment of history v, and the time before every moment at which one is present is of finite duration on the clock k (MetricGrimReaper.MetricallyFinitePast: the clock readings of all moments at or before it, populated or not, are bounded below). The intended clock is the physically privileged one, CLOCK_1 (cosmic or proper time); with a bounded clock every past is finite and BEGINS_2 reduces to the history being populated. It constrains time, not contingent reality: it does not say when contingent reality began. Examples: discrete or continuous time with a first moment; a populated past that is open below and of finite duration, the order and metric shape of standard FLRW cosmic time (the initial singularity is not a moment). Non-examples: an endless succession of populated days; integer time that is empty before 0 and populated from 0 on, in which contingent reality began a finite time ago but the time before it is infinite. Nothing is said about a first moment, an empty moment or a cause.
note: Analyst metric sense; attribution deferred. Relative to the supplied TimeClock and not invariant under reparametrization (CLOCK disambiguation 725f3417-73d0-489f-b8ab-7b2628ff36b7): under ln t an FLRW past is infinite and under arctan an integer past is finite; the CLOCK_1 reading is an OPEN commitment. One clock serves every world of the frame. Strictly weaker than BEGINS_1 in linear time (possiblyFiniteDurationOfFirstMoment; converse fails in MetricBeginningArrival control 2). It is the sense on which the metric Grim Reaper conclusion (PopulatedPastsMetricallyFinite) bears. It is not the unformalized sense of a first populated moment after emptiness.
